visualTeachingNotes: A mature mother figure in the 女-type kneeling/side-view posture, with arms folded or crossed in front.

Regular 母 squares the body and preserves the two internal marks as the characteristic dots or short strokes inside the modern form.

recognitionTakeaway: This picture shows a high-footed lidded vessel, not a bean. The vessel’s name sounded like the word for beans, so its picture was borrowed to write that word; this sound-based meaning became dominant, while the vessel meaning survived mainly in historical contexts.
visualTeachingNotes: A lidded pedestal vessel—the object depicted by the old pictograph, rather than a modern bean.
Oracle clearly shows a bowl or vessel resting on a narrow stand and broad foot.
Regular 豆 preserves the stacked vessel structure as a top lid, central container, narrow support, and bottom strokes even though the everyday meaning later shifted to “bean.”
